title: POC scoping - Quality eval plan
summary: Initial POC scoping to align on success criteria, workload sizing, benchmark plan, timelines, and quality evaluation methodology (golden prompts, regression, hallucination checks, scoring). Agreed on a 4-week technical POC with explicit quality gates and benchmark targets; Redwood to send detailed eval plan and share test harness + pricing options.
next_steps: Redwood to send Quality Eval Plan doc and example golden prompts (Samir) - due 2026-08-24
NovaHealth to provide sample dataset / 500 de-identified records (Aisha) - due 2026-08-28
Schedule benchmark run (bench env) week of 2026-08-31 (Lena + Sara)
Sign minimal NDA / data access form (Devon) - due 2026-08-25
action_items: Samir: Share detailed eval plan + pricing matrix (due 2026-08-24)
Aisha: Export & de-identify sample dataset (500 records) (due 2026-08-28)
Devon: Confirm security requirements + KMS details (due 2026-08-25)
Sara: Schedule engineering kickoff and provide cluster access details (due 2026-08-30)
transcript:
Meeting header: 2026-08-21 15:00 UTC | Duration: 42 minutes | Attendees: Samir (Redwood AE), Lena (Redwood SE), Marco (Redwood SE), Priya (CSM), Aisha (Head of ML - NovaHealth), Tom (PM), Sara (Eng Manager), Devon (Security)

[00:00] Samir: alright hey everyone thanks for joining, uh this is Samir from Redwood, i'll hand it to lena and marco to go into the technical eval plan but first quick round - who we have?
[00:06] Aisha: hi this is aisha, head of ml at novahealth, my team's responsible for clinical summarization pipelines, and we're looking to validate an LLM for safe summarization and triage.
[00:12] Tom: tom here, product, timeline is tight - board asked for a pilot in q4, so hoping for clear pass/fail criteria.
[00:18] Sara: sara engineering, will run the infra and help with data exports and benchmarking.
[00:22] Devon: devon security - i'll need SOC2/ISO details, kms, and data residency notes.
[00:27] Lena: great thanks. goal for today's call: align on POC scope and especially the quality evaluation plan — golden prompts, regression tests, hallucination and format checks, scoring. we'll propose a 3-4 week POC with a set of gates. sound good?
[00:36] Aisha: yes, that's what we need. we have two core use cases: clinical note summarization and patient message triage. accuracy + hallucination avoidance are top priorities.
[00:44] Marco: noted. quick question about throughput - what's your expected qps or batch size in POC?
[00:49] Sara: for the POC we'll start small — about 500 requests/day, each request avg 800 tokens, but production plans are 2k-3k reqs/day. we want to see latency and cost per 1k tokens.
[01:00] Lena: that's helpful. for sizing we'll run benchmarks at three profiles: small (500 reqs/day), medium (2k/day), and burst (5k/day) to measure latency p95 and cost.
[01:09] Samir: on success criteria, propose two parallel tracks: quality and performance. quality: F1/ROUGE-like target on golden prompts and human-evaluated hallucination rate < 2% on clinical facts. performance: p95 latency < 650ms for hosted model variant or < 300ms on dedicated setup for trimmed prompts. does that align?
[01:24] Tom: that seems reasonable but we need to define how hallucination is measured. also what's the scoring approach?
[01:29] Lena: our scoring approach will be a mix: automated metrics (ROUGE, BLEU where applicable) + a human evaluation rubric. we recommend a 5-point scale for clinical correctness, a binary hallucination flag per output, and a format compliance score for structure (e.g., JSON schema). aggregated score = weighted sum: 50% clinical correctness, 30% hallucination rate (lower is better), 20% format compliance.
[01:50] Aisha: can you share an example rubric?
[01:52] Lena: yes we'll include a sample rubric in the eval plan doc. sample: 5 = perfect, 4 = minor omission, 3 = several omissions but no clinical error, 2 = incorrect clinical assertion, 1 = dangerous clinically incorrect. hallucination flag if any unsupported clinical assertion appears.
[02:06] Marco: for golden prompts, we want to lock down 25 representative prompts per use case — those will be manually annotated by nova clinicians and locked as ground truth. we'll run these every night as regression tests.
[02:17] Sara: 25 per use case sounds ok. can we add edge-case prompts? we have some messy notes.
[02:21] Lena: absolutely, we recommend 10 edge cases per use case focusing on abbreviations, missing context, and adversarial phrasing.
[02:28] Tom: ok so regression tests = nightly runs of the golden set, compare to previous baseline, alert if aggregate score drops > 3 points?
[02:35] Priya: and we'll set up automated diffs and visualizations in Redwood Console to show token-level deltas and sample failures.
[02:41] Aisha: what about hallucination checks specifically? can you do rule-based fact extraction to validate?
[02:46] Lena: yes we can do simple fact-check rules for structured clinical facts (medication names, dosages, dates). for free-text assertions we'll rely on human review on a sampled subset; we can also run a second-model verification step — but that'll be part of the POC scope decision (extra cost).
[02:58] Devon: security question - data residency and kms. can we run POC on dedicated private deployment or do we need hosted?
[03:04] Samir: by default POC can run on hosted sandbox with encrypted storage and transient logs; for regulated PHI we'd recommend a dedicated or private deployment — we can provide a short-term Dedicated pool for the POC if required, Redwood will share the Private deployment checklist.
[03:16] Devon: i'll need SOC2 evidence, encryption in transit + at rest, and option for customer-managed KMS.
[03:22] Samir: yes we'll include SOC2 report and KMS integration docs in the packet we send.
[03:25] Aisha: timeline — you mentioned 3-4 weeks. can you lay out milestones?
[03:29] Lena: proposed timeline: Week 0 (this week): agree eval plan, exchange golden prompts and sample data. Week 1: infra setup + one-off smoke runs. Week 2: benchmark runs across sizes + nightly regression start. Week 3: human eval sampling and final scoring, decision meeting end of week 3. if we need a dedicated setup add 1 week for networking.
[03:44] Tom: so end-to-end about 3 weeks if no private infra needed. okay.
[03:47] Marco: for benchmarks we will report p50/p95 latency, throughput, cost per 1k tokens, peak concurrency profile, and failure modes. We'll also surface KV cache hit rates and bunlded batching effects; note that quantized variants may change quality slightly.
[04:00] Aisha: on scoring thresholds — what aggregate score would you recommend as a pass?
[04:04] Lena: recommend initial pass threshold aggregated >= 80/100 with hallucination rate under 2% and no critical clinical errors in human sample. we can tune weights with NovaHealth later.
[04:14] Sara: can we set up an automated embargoed dashboard for stakeholders?
[04:17] Priya: yes Redwood Console can create per-route dashboards; we'll give NovaHealth viewers and exportable reports.
[04:22] Tom: what about false negatives in triage? we need precision high for urgent items.
[04:27] Lena: for triage we'll add precision/recall targets: precision >= 90% for urgent label, recall target 85% (we can prioritize precision if you prefer).
[04:36] Aisha: are there known tradeoffs between latency and hallucination? like does batching or quantization increase hallucination risk?
[04:41] Marco: quantization sometimes increases minor fluency issues and in edge cases may alter factuality; we'll include quantization A/B tests in benchmark plan and monitor quality deltas in regression. batching generally doesn't change output quality but can mask token-level prompt truncation issues — we'll test at realistic sequence lengths.
[04:58] Devon: about cost — what estimate for a 3-week POC on hosted vs dedicated?
[05:02] Samir: rough ballpark: hosted POC ~ $6-8k depending on model family and token volume; short Dedicated trial with reserved capacity ~ $12-15k (includes small dedicated pool). we'll share a pricing matrix.
[05:12] Tom: okay send pricing and an example contract.
[05:15] Samir: will do.
[05:16] Lena: a couple operational notes for the eval plan doc: 1) provide canonical golden prompt list and expected output format (we'll validate JSON schema), 2) provide annotation guide for human raters, 3) define nightly regression alert thresholds, 4) provide sample scoring spreadsheet and visualization template.
[05:31] Aisha: that covers it. one more question: can you redact PHI automatically before sending to Redwood? we prefer to share de-identified samples but may need help.
[05:39] Sara: we have a de-id script but might need support for edge cases.
[05:42] Marco: Redwood can run a de-id preprocessor as part of the pipeline for the POC under a data processing addendum; we'll include options in the doc.
[05:49] Tom: ok great. next steps recap?
[05:52] Samir: recap: 1) Samir send Eval Plan + pricing + SOC2 docs + golden prompts template by 2026-08-24. 2) NovaHealth to provide 500 de-identified records and 25 golden prompts per use case by 2026-08-28. 3) Lena to provision bench env and run initial smoke tests week of 2026-08-31. 4) Devon to confirm security checks and NDA by 2026-08-25. 5) schedule decision meeting for 2026-09-17 to review results.
[06:15] Aisha: sounds good, thanks everyone.
[06:17] Samir: thanks all, we'll follow up with docs and calendar invites.
[06:20] (call ends)
notes: Agreed 3-week POC with optional dedicated week for Private infra
Golden prompts: 25 per use case + 10 edge cases
Scoring: weighted aggregate (50% clinical correctness, 30% hallucination rate, 20% format compliance)
